title: Viewport tiling & deferred interaction for high-density time-series
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Reduce initial paint and interaction cost for pages that render very large time-series (10k+ points) while preserving keyboard/touch accessibility and legend/tooltip parity. We will introduce a viewport-tiling render strategy (divide series into horizontal tiles based on visible time range), deferred interaction layers (render static canvas tiles first, mount interactive overlay only for focused/hovered regions), and token-driven theming for contrast-safe mini-legend states. The ticket covers design specs, small prototypes (canvas + SVG hybrid), accessibility notes, and handoff artifacts for engineering to implement batching-friendly rendering hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Initial page load for a 50-series, 100k-point dataset renders visible viewport within 300ms on a mid-tier laptop (measured by perf lab), with progressive tile loading for offscreen ranges
Keyboard navigation can focus series entries in the mini-legend and reveal tooltip content via Enter/Space; ARIA live region announces significant changes without repeating token counts
Tooltips and legends match current design parity (exact copy of tooltip schema) and work when interactive overlay is mounted; fallback tooltip works for canvas-only mode
Design tokens for chart colors, disabled/low-contrast states, and focus rings are documented in the tokens page and a migration guide for components is provided
Storybook examples demonstrating: tiled rendering, deferred overlay, touch scrub gesture on tile boundaries, and an a11y test harness with VoiceOver/JAWS scenarios
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Kapoor: Kickoff notes. Discovery showed CPU spikes from repainting full SVG on pan/zoom. Proposal: break series into 256px tiles horizontally and render those as separate canvas layers to limit repaints.

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Built a quick POC using canvas tiling + pointer-events overlay. POC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/1234. Initial perf numbers promising (40% fewer main-thread paints).

2026-03-06 - Accessibility review (June Park): Ensure focus order aligns with DOM reading order; use a dedicated ARIA live region for viewport changes and avoid verbose announcements during scrubbing. Also recommend visible focus ring tokens and keyboard-exposed tooltip show/hide semantics.

2026-03-07 - PM feedback (Marco Alvarez): This must be backward compatible for existing dashboards. Add a migration path and toggle to opt into tiling per panel. Consider a runtime flag in Console for gradual rollout.

2026-03-09 - Design decision: Use hybrid canvas for series rendering + SVG/HTML for overlays (legend, annotations). Rationale: canvas reduces repaint cost; SVG/HTML gives accessible DOM for focus and semantics.

2026-03-11 - Engineering sync (Kavita Rao): Need API hooks for incremental tile hydration so runtime can batch KV cache warm-up and avoid duplicative model/worker handoffs. Kavita will open ENG-3219 to add the runtime API endpoint.

2026-03-12 - Prototype user test: Touch scrub felt laggy when overlay mounted eagerly. Updated plan: defer overlay mounting until pointer stops for 80ms or explicit focus via keyboard. Added 'deferredInteractionDelay' token (default 80ms) to tokens doc.

2026-03-13 - Asha: Preparing final handoff docs. Added Storybook stories and accessibility checklist. Linking design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Viewport+Tiling+Spec and implementation ticket ENG-3219.
Post-merge checklist: update CHANGELOG, add runtime feature flag, coordinate rollout with console release 2026.04
